processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: As-cast ingot (vacuum induction melted under high-purity Ar) homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h; identical route applied to all four Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr alloys.
Ingots hot-rolled to 4 mm-thick sheets with 95% thickness reduction; initial rolling temperature 1040–1060 °C and finishing rolling temperature 950–970 °C.

processing_steps.method: online ultrafast cooling (UFC) using in-house ADCOS-PM efficient-use-water device
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The hot-rolled plate was online ultrafast cooled (UFCed) to ambient temperature at a cooling rate of ~40 °C/s; this is the final step producing the UFCed (as-received) state labelled 2Ni.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized, single-phase equiaxed face-centred cubic (FCC) γ austenite containing a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries; no B2 (BCC) phase detected by EBSD or XRD. Ni-rich nanoscale κ-carbides (and no detectable LRO domains) are distributed in the γ matrix.

phases_present.volume_fraction: single phase (~100%, essentially fully red in EBSD phase maps)
phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with annealing twins / high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries
phases_present.grain_size: 8.95 μm (excluding twin boundaries); 3.73 μm (including twin boundaries)
phases_present.texture: no strong texture (equiaxed grains in mixed colours)

phases_present.volume_fraction: very low (low superlattice intensity; quantitative estimate not possible from DF)

precipitates.distribution: homogeneously distributed in the γ matrix (orthorhombic κ-carbides)
precipitates.coherency: coherent with the γ austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: Deformation substructure of the 2Ni steel, dominated by planar slip. With increasing strain, planar slip bands multiply and the spacing between them refines; near final failure high-density dislocations, very fine slip bands and a small number of stacking faults appear, but no deformation twins were detected throughout plastic deformation.

microstructure_list.region: gauge section (RD), interrupted tensile specimens at 5%, 10% and close to final failure (LD)

phases_present.morphology: grains with planar slip bands, refined slip bands and stacking faults

defects.type: dislocation slip bands (planar slip on (1-11), (−111) and (200) planes; [011](1-11), [011](−111) and [011](200) systems)
high-density dislocations and very fine slip bands near final failure

precipitates.distribution: wavy, banded/modulated distribution in the matrix

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent (coherent nano κ-carbides in austenite; ductility largely unimpaired due to coherence between κ-carbides and austenite)

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation shearing of κ-carbide precipitates / planar slip penetrating grains and cutting through κ-carbides
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In 2Ni steel, residual dislocation planar slip after deformation penetrates the grain and cuts through the κ-carbides; the shearing (shear-strengthening) mechanism is the predominant precipitate-dislocation interaction, giving ordering, coherency and modulus-mismatch strengthening contributions.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip is the primary deformation mode of the 2Ni steel; slip bands are relatively uniformly distributed and multiply with increasing strain while their spacing decreases. Three groups of slip systems form: [011](1-11), [011](−111) and [011](200). Near final failure, high-density dislocations, very fine slip bands and a small number of stacking faults are present, but no deformation twins were detected throughout the entire plastic deformation.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Ni addition lowers the κ-carbide formation energy and promotes the nucleation/growth of Ni-rich κ-carbides (AlNi3C structure), and no deformation-induced phase transformation (e.g. twinning) is reported for 2Ni steel.
interfaces.interface_notes: κ-carbide volume fraction is very low and could not be quantified from dark-field images because the foil thickness is uncertain; only the κ-carbide/austenite coherent interface is relevant for 2Ni steel.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge length 25 mm, thickness 3 mm, width 7 mm, cut by EDM along the rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: At least three tensile specimens of each steel were deformed to fracture to ensure reproducibility; interrupted tests to engineering strains of 3% (or 5%) and 10%

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering and true stress–strain curves for 2Ni steel (red curve, Fig. 4a,b); engineering curve peaks just above 1200 MPa and terminates near strain 0.33; true stress terminates earliest near ~0.25 true strain
strain_hardening_rate: Three strain-hardening stages (I, II, III); Stage I sharp decrease, Stage II increase, Stage III decrease; strain-hardening rate of 2Ni drops to zero near true strain 0.25 (earliest of the four steels)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, thickness 3 mm, width 7 mm

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Total elongation: the 2Ni5Cr steel shows an increment of ~16% in total elongation compared with the no-Cr steel (i.e. the 2Ni steel, used here as the Cr-free baseline)

Ni/Cr synergy: the 2Ni steel has the highest yield strength (1202 MPa) and ultimate tensile strength (1283 MPa) among the four UFCed Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr steels; addition of Cr to the 2Ni-based steels lowers yield strength (1202→1071 MPa) and tensile strength (1283→1187 MPa) while raising total elongation (34.1→54.5%)

lifetime_prediction.model_used: Linear superposition yield-strength model σys = σ0 + σss + σgb + σprep

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Calculated versus measured yield strength for the 2Ni steel: calculated mechanism contributions (σ0 ≈ 42 MPa, σgb ≈ 231.3 MPa, σss ≈ 509.5 MPa, σprep) sum below the experimental YS of 1202 MPa; the experimental value lies above the calculated bar in Fig. 11

characterization_methods.technique: Electron back-scatter diffraction (EBSD) – IPF maps and phase maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Ultra55 scanning electron microscope; specimens vibration-polished with 50 nm colloidal silica for 2.5–24 h in a Buehler-VibroMet 2
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: as-UFCed (undeformed) plate section; 20 µm scale-bar IPF and phase maps
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine microstructure, phase constitution, twin-boundary fraction and average grain size (excluding/including twin boundaries) of the 2Ni steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni steel is fully recrystallized single equiaxed FCC γ austenite with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries and no B2 phase; average grain sizes 8.95 μm (excluding twins) and 3.73 μm (including twins)
2Ni steel shows only the five FCC austenite reflections γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311) and γ(222); no B2/BCC reflection present, confirming single-phase γ austenite

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) bright-field imaging with selected-area electron diffraction (SADP)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 operating at 200 kV; specimens thinned by Struers TenuPol-3 electrochemical double-jet (10 vol% perchloric acid + 90 vol% ethanol, 20 V, −30 °C)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 1 µm scale-bar bright-field images; SADP along the [011]γ zone axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm the γ austenite matrix, twins and dislocation structure of the 2Ni steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni microstructure is all γ austenite phase with annealing twins and dislocation lines; SADP indexed on [011]γ with weak κ spots (011κ, 100κ)

characterization_methods.technique: TEM dark-field (DF) imaging and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) with FFT/IFFT analysis
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 TEM; Image-Pro Plus software for >200 domain measurements
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: DF taken from {110}κ reflections (20 nm scale bar); HRTEM along [011]γ (10 nm scale bar); IFFT from {011} and {100} superlattice reflections
characterization_methods.purpose: Image and measure the κ-carbides / LRO domains in the 2Ni steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni steel contains the largest, brightest cuboidal κ-carbides of the four steels with an average size of 10 nm (IFFT/Image-Pro Plus value ~10.69 nm); the ordered structures are κ-carbides (not LRO domains)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: fibre zone of the fracture surface; 200 µm scale bar; macroscopic fracture-surface insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the fracture mode of the 2Ni steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni steel fibre zone shows a dense dimpled microvoid-coalescence morphology with larger, deeper rounded holes and rough tear ridges, i.e. ductile fracture with no cleavage facets

characterization_methods.technique: Uniaxial tensile testing with laser extensometer; interrupted tensile tests
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Gotech electronic universal testing machine; laser extensometer; specimens cut by electrical discharge machining (EDM)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: crosshead speed 3 mm/min; gauge length 25 mm, thickness 3 mm, width 7 mm; along RD; at least three specimens per steel; interrupted at 3% (or 5%) and 10% engineering strain
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure room-temperature tensile properties and provide interrupted specimens for substructure analysis of the 2Ni steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni steel: YS 1202 MPa, TS 1283 MPa, TEL 34.1%, TS×TEL 43.75 GPa-%

computational_details.simulation_method: First-principles (DFT) formation-energy calculations of possible κ-carbide structures
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Density functional theory (DFT) with generalized gradient approximation (GGA) and Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) functional
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated formation-energy trend (Ni lowers, Cr raises the κ-carbide formation energy) is stated to be consistent with the dark-field TEM images of Fig. 1i–1l showing that Ni-containing steels have larger κ-carbides.

analytical_models.equation_role: Determines whether Ni-rich κ-carbides are energetically favourable to form and the lowering of the nucleation barrier

parameters.name: formation energy of Cr-rich carbide Cr21(FeC3)2

analytical_models.model_note: For the 2Ni steel, Ni atoms preferentially displace Fe/Mn atoms to form Ni-rich κ-carbides with AlNi3C structure; its formation energy (−0.181 eV/atom) is lower than that of ideal κ-carbides (−0.160 eV/atom), reducing the nucleation energy barrier and promoting κ-carbide formation and growth; Fe2NiC (0.082 eV/atom) is unfavourable. Cr21(FeC3)2 (−0.049 eV/atom) is 0.111 eV/atom higher than (Fe,Mn)3AlC, raising the nucleation barrier for Cr-containing steels.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening-mechanism model of yield strength (linear superposition of mechanisms)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated contributions are compared with the experimentally measured YS of the 2Ni steel (1202 MPa); predicted and measured yield strengths are stated to be in very good agreement (experimental value lies above the summed calculated contributions in Fig. 11).

analytical_models.equation_role: σys = σ0 + σss + σgb + σprep (Eq. 1); dislocation strengthening disregarded for fully recrystallized steel

parameters.name: σ0 (friction stress, = 3τ0, τ0 = 2×10^-4 G with G = 70 GPa)

analytical_models.model_note: d_eff values (3.51, 3.73, 3.72, 2.2 μm for 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr) from EBSD; calculated σgb = 238.5, 231.3, 231.7 and 301.2 MPa respectively.
Calculated σss = 515.4, 509.5, 557.2 and 554.1 MPa for 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr respectively.

analytical_models.model_name: Precipitation strengthening by shearing (ordering + coherency + modulus mismatch)
analytical_models.equation_role: σprep = max(σorder, σcoh + σmod) (Eqs. 2–4); shearing is the dominant mechanism as dislocations shear the κ-carbides
analytical_models.model_note: For the 2Ni steel σcoh+σmod is dominant and no σorder bars appear (Fig. 10b); the size distribution and volume fraction of κ-carbides are used to compute σprep, which is then compared with the experimental YS.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 2Ni steel (Table 1, wt.%): C 1.23, Si 0.35, Mn 21.0, P 0.010, S 0.001, Al 9.35, Mo 0.57, Ni 2.05, Cr 0.05, Ti 0.01, Nb 0.03, Fe Bal. (nominal Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-2Ni, x = 2 wt% Ni, y = 0 wt% Cr).
TS × TEL of the 2Ni steel is 43.75 GPa-%, the lowest TS×TEL combination among the four 'This study' steels (3Cr 62.07, 2Ni 43.75, 2Ni3Cr 55.36, 2Ni5Cr 59.94 GPa-%).

The volume fraction of κ-carbides in the 2Ni steel is very low (low superlattice diffraction intensity) and a quantitative estimate could not be given from dark-field images because the sheet/foil thickness is uncertain.

No deformation twins were detected throughout the entire plastic deformation of the 2Ni steel; its strain hardenability mainly benefits from the DSBR (dynamic slip band refinement) effect, and a small number of stacking faults appear only at very high strain near final failure.

The 2Ni steel has the largest κ-carbides (and the highest yield strength) of the four Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr steels; the average κ-carbide/LRO domain sizes of the series decrease from ~10.69 nm (2Ni) through ~5.46 nm (2Ni3Cr) and ~2.14 nm (2Ni5Cr) to ~1.75 nm (3Cr).

SADPs of the 2Ni steel were labelled [011]γ//[011]κ with primary γ spots (000γ, 111γ, 200γ) plus weaker κ spots (011κ, 100κ); the paper caption states the SADPs were taken along the [001]γ zone axis, which disagrees with the [011] zone-axis labels printed on the patterns.

Ni addition to the 2Ni steel has an equivalent atomic-radius argument: Ni (1.24 Å) and Fe (1.27 Å)/Mn (1.32 Å) radii are comparable, so Ni preferentially displaces Fe/Mn to form Ni-rich κ-carbides, and this reduces the κ-carbide formation energy and enlarges the κ-carbides.
